note: Not a skill: the background-wait mechanics the always-on quality-gates rule carried until audit 2026-10-14 RU04 moved them to the shell dispatcher's note on the first background call. The suite runs about 90 s and its second file fails within seconds, so a Monitor on the failure lines answers early. Every step quotes the sentence it grades, in the rule or the note. In a real session (conformance.js, per turn) the three steps tied to the replay's suite and its failing test are session: false, so a turn that ran no suite fails nothing; the two others grade every turn.

prompts.explicit: Run the full test suite (npm test, about 90 seconds) in the background, watch it the way the quality-gates rule says, and tell me which test fails and why.
prompts.plain: Run npm test - it takes a minute or two - and tell me which test fails and why.
prompts.adverse: The tests are slow, just kick off npm test and tell me what breaks.

steps.quote: A wait measured in MINUTES (a CI run, a container build, a full suite, an emulator boot) runs in the background

graders.name: the suite runs in the background
